description: REGRESSION WALL for saga #811, flipped by issue #815 from the characterization issue #1087 built against the broken build. The THIRD fault class — a name that IS registered but has no evaluator behind it. It is neither of the two shapes issue #816 characterizes: shape A's name is not registered at all, and shape B's is registered *and* evaluable (its fault is positional). `challenge` is registered by `@openlogo/parser`'s Tutor primitive table, correctly kinded a Command, and `@openlogo/runtime` has no evaluator for it. This is the class the #814 ruling's `ol-not-implemented` code exists for, and nothing in the corpus exercised it before these fixtures. The `check()` half. It used to report `ol-unknown-command` — a code whose learner message is about a name that is *not known* — for a name this implementation registered and this specification defines, blaming the learner for its own omission. `spec/error-model.md:131` forbids exactly that, "at ANY stage, including by withholding it from the visible vocabulary so that the call reads as unknown", which is verbatim the mechanism `checker-names.ts` used; #815 deleted it. The name now resolves and its arity is correct, so the checker has nothing to say: **the expectation is an EMPTY diagnostics list**, and that emptiness is the assertion. **Read the modality before reading this fixture as the contract.** `spec/error-model.md:131` makes `ol-not-implemented`'s stage a **MAY** at `semantic` — "when the implementation knows before running that no evaluation exists" — and a **MUST** at `runtime` otherwise. This implementation declines the MAY, and declining it is fully conformant: whether an evaluation exists is a fact about `@openlogo/runtime`, which `@openlogo/parser` — the package that owns the semantic stage — must not depend on. So an implementation reporting this at `semantic` is equally conformant, and a reader must not take the `runtime` recorded here for a requirement. `spec/tooling.md:194` says the same thing from the checker's side — report it here "only when the checker knows before running that no evaluation exists; otherwise it is the run's to report" — so silence here is the correct counterpart of the `runtime` answer its `-execute` sibling records.
